name: Five-claim factuality/coherence pair (Voyager 1 plasma instrument)
source: authored: docs/iclr2027/coherence worked example (5 claims, 3 true + 2 false, priors 0.9/0.1)
notes: The paper's headline worked pair. ONE claim set of five atoms, three true (prior 0.9) and two false (prior 0.1), realized by TWO responses over the same claims. Response A is logically coherent: it asserts the three true claims as a support chain and explicitly attributes-and-rejects the two false ones. Response B is logically incoherent: it asserts the same five claims but leans on a false claim as a load-bearing premise and contradicts its own chain. Exact by 2^5 = 32-world enumeration; see scripts/lcs_worked_pair.py. A: LCS_mm 0.5905, LCS_cons 0.9625, log Z -0.952. B: LCS_mm 0.4938, LCS_cons 0.4136, log Z -3.780. In B the TRUE claim a3 is dragged from 0.992 to 0.513 -- below its own 0.9 prior -- which is the per-claim diagnostic no aggregate score reveals. Response A's prose was rewritten for flow (2026-09-09): the meta-signpost and the doubled "It is sometimes said / It is also said" gave way to an ordinary enumeration, and the a3->a5 refusal now cites the Oort cloud's gravitational binding rather than merely its distance. The relation set, the priors and every expected value are UNCHANGED -- the rewrite holds all four of A's gold_relations fixed, which is why scripts/lcs_worked_pair.py still reproduces the same numbers. Both responses answer one query: "Where is Voyager 1 now, and has it left the Solar System?" (shown in Figure 1 of docs/iclr2027/coherence; not a field here, since the model scores responses standalone).

atoms.text: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in August 2012.
atoms.label: a1

atoms.text: After the crossing, Voyager 1's instruments measured a sharp rise in plasma density.
atoms.label: a2

atoms.text: Voyager 1 is therefore in interstellar space.
atoms.label: a3

atoms.text: Voyager 1's plasma wave instrument failed permanently before the crossing.
atoms.label: a4

atoms.text: Voyager 1 has left the Solar System entirely.
atoms.label: a5

A.label: coherent
A.response: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in August 2012, and in the days that followed its instruments measured a sharp rise in plasma density -- the signature of the denser medium beyond, and the measurement that established the boundary had been passed. Voyager 1 is therefore in interstellar space. Two persistent misconceptions are worth clearing up. The first is that the probe's plasma wave instrument had failed permanently before the crossing; it cannot have, since it is precisely that instrument which returned the density profile the conclusion rests on. The second is that Voyager 1 has left the Solar System altogether. Being in interstellar space is not the same thing: the Sun's gravitational reach extends through the Oort cloud, far beyond the probe's present distance.

B.label: incoherent
B.response: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in August 2012, and after the crossing its instruments measured a sharp rise in plasma density. That said, the probe cannot really be counted as being in interstellar space. The plasma wave instrument had in fact failed permanently before the crossing, and it is precisely that failure which tells us the probe reached interstellar space. The instrument failure also means Voyager 1 has left the Solar System entirely. Of course, the August 2012 crossing rules out any such permanent failure, and the density measurement is flatly inconsistent with the probe having left the Solar System.
